_about: Field terms for F97, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

scpdsi.definition: a monthly drought index computed from temperature and precipitation through a simple soil water balance, with its constants calibrated to each location so values compare across places
scpdsi.excludes: a direct measurement of soil moisture or of streamflow

chronology.definition: one yearly series for a site, built by dating many cores, removing each core's age and size trend and averaging the results into a dimensionless index
chronology.excludes: a single core's raw ring widths, and a climate reconstruction made from the series

space-band.field: signal processing on irregular sites, our usage
space-band.definition: the part of a field that varies between two spatial scales, taken as the difference of two Gaussian smoothings of the site values with the two scales as widths; the six bands add back to the field
space-band.excludes: an exact wavenumber, because the bands overlap and the sites are irregular

time-band.definition: the part of a yearly series whose period lies between two limits, kept by masking its Fourier transform
time-band.excludes: a moving average or a fitted trend

squared-coherence.definition: the share of one series' variance in a frequency band that a linear filter of the other series can account for, between 0 and 1; here pooled over sites and years in each space and time band and called the passed share
squared-coherence.excludes: a nonlinear dependence, and the size of the response, which the gain measures

separable.definition: a covariance that factors into a function of distance times a function of time lag, so the spatial pattern of correlation has the same shape at every lag
separable.excludes: fields whose anomalies travel or whose broad and fine patterns fade at different rates

dispersion-exponent.definition: the power beta in a decay rate that grows as the wavenumber to the power beta; diffusion gives about 2, and fine and broad patterns that fade at the same rate give 0
dispersion-exponent.excludes: a speed of travel, which the propagation test measures

phase-randomisation.definition: a copy of a series with the same power spectrum and random Fourier phases, so it keeps the series' autocorrelation and loses its timing against any other series
phase-randomisation.excludes: shuffling years, which also destroys the autocorrelation

block-bootstrap.definition: an interval made by recomputing a statistic many times on years resampled in runs of consecutive years, here 10, so that year-to-year correlation is kept inside each run
block-bootstrap.excludes: resampling single years as if they were independent

benjamini-hochberg.definition: a rule that adjusts a set of p values so that, among the tests called significant, the expected share of false calls stays at or below a chosen rate q, here 0.05
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: the stricter Bonferroni rule, which bounds the chance of any false call
